newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end narrowly mixed, seen soft.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end narrowly mixed, seen soft.

text.p: Argentine stocks hovered in a narrow range Wednesday and closed virtually flat, with most investors still on the sidelines and focused on U.S. economic indicators, dealers said.

"Players remain hesitant ahead of the U.S. elections (Tuesday)," said Adolfo Adorno of Agra traders. "Many are waiting for the local bond market to consolidate after recent gains before taking up positions in stocks."
The blue-chip MerVal index closed unchanged at 570.23, after a 1.4 percent rise Tuesday, while the broad market index dipped 0.2 percent.

"The stock and bond markets are taking different cues," said trader Roberto Diaz at local bank Socimer. "I'd say the stock market will fall slightly more this week and then start a strong upward movement."
He said investors were very cautiously building up their stock portfolios, while bonds grabbed the spotlight due to the rally Tuesday in U.S. Treasuries.

The U.S. long bond yield, after hitting 6.64 percent early in the session, recovered Wednesday to 6.71 percent against 6.68 percent at the close Tuesday, when the market soared. "We should expect more of this volatility," said Adorno.
Floor volume dwindled to 13.5 million pesos from 21.7 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals totalled 64.6 million pesos against 87.8 million Tuesday.
Losers edged out winners 22 to 21 in the session and 25 issues closed flat.

Strongest main-tier rises were in Banco Frances and agricultural holding company Cresud, which jumped 3.4 percent and 2.3 percent respectively. Worst performers were holding company Comercial del Plata, which dropped 3.3 percent, and Telefonica and Telecom, both off 1.1 percent.
